paragraphs: Rabbi Uziel, son of Rabbi Nehunya, of Berat Havran [printed: דברת חוורן].

Hyman cites the end of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:7 and the supplied Beitzah locator ל״ג ה״ב [compare 3:2] for Rabbi Chizkiyah reporting in Uziel’s name. In Maaser Sheni, Hyman says, the text mistakenly reads R’ Yechezkel. Moed Katan 5a gives the teaching in the name of R’ Uziel, grandson of R’ Uziel the Elder.

notes.text: בר בריה means grandson, as the complete Moed Katan5a paragraph confirms. The Beitzah locator ל״ג ה״ב remains malformed or unresolved; no chapter number is invented. The notice separately records Chizkiyah versus Yechezkel.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Beitzah3:2 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Chizkiyah followed by Rabbi Uziel son of Rabbi Chunya of Berat Chavran, without an explicit intermediate reporting connector. It identifies the matching location beside supplied ל״ג ה״ב, but does not prove a lamed/pe print error or erase Nehunya versus Chunya. The earlier Shabbat and MoedKatan consultations are inherited; בר בריה means grandson, not bar followed by son. Hyman’s Yechezkel-is-an-error claim in MaaserSheni remains attributed, not newly proven correction history. Uninspected MoedKatan personal titles remain abbreviated.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:7 joins Chizkiyah and Uziel with “and,” while Beitzah 3:2 puts their names side by side. Both call Uziel the son of Chunya of Berat Chavran. In Maaser Sheni 5:1, the Guggenheimer text has Chizkiyah, while the Vilna-based text published by Daat has Yechezkel. Both put the named sage beside Uziel and give the teaching in Chunya’s name. Daat’s wording explicitly has them speak together. The judgment that Yechezkel is an error is Hyman’s. Bavli Moed Katan 5a attributes the parallel grave-marking teaching to Uziel, grandson of Uziel the Elder.
